subject: Career
title: You Already Have a Brand
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on You Already Have a Brand.

hook.text: Google your name. Whatever comes up — that's your personal brand, whether you built it or not.

buildup.text: A personal brand is what people say about you when you're not in the room.

discovery.text: Jeff Bezos coined that definition. Your reputation precedes you in every job and opportunity.

twist.text: If you don't shape your brand, others will. And they'll use whatever fragments they find.

climax.text: A personal brand isn't vanity — it's professional insurance. It opens doors before you knock.

punchline.text: You don't choose to have a brand. You choose to shape it.

quiz.question: Who defined personal brand as 'what people say about you when you're not in the room'?

details.summary: Whether you have cultivated it or not, people already form perceptions about you based on your work, communication style, and online presence. Your personal brand exists by default; the only question is whether you manage it intentionally.
details.whyItMatters: Ignoring your personal brand does not mean it does not exist. It means others are defining it for you, often inaccurately, which can limit career opportunities you never know about.
takeaways: Your brand is what people say about you when you leave the room
Default brands form from scattered impressions and assumptions
Intentional brand management aligns perception with reality

faq.question: How do you discover what your current personal brand actually is?
faq.answer: Ask five to ten colleagues and contacts to describe you in three words. Google your name and review what appears. The gap between how you want to be perceived and how others actually describe you reveals exactly where brand management is needed.

faq.question: Is personal branding only important for people in public-facing roles?
faq.answer: No. Every professional benefits from an intentional brand because hiring managers, collaborators, and leaders form impressions regardless of your role. Even engineers and analysts advance faster when their expertise and reliability are consistently visible.
